integrity: The dimension-one/two statement is proved analytically by the exact Newton–Schulz polynomial and monotonicity of its scalar transfer function. The dimension-three obstruction is an exact rational witness. The bundled checker verifies the finite algebra but is not used to infer the universal two-dimensional theorem.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to exact-arithmetic Newton–Schulz inversion, scalar initialization, symmetric positive definite Stieltjes matrices, and the standard spectral convergence range. It does not cover nonsymmetric M-matrices, arbitrary initial matrices, dropping, rounding, or other hyperpower schemes.
title: Three dimensions are minimal for transient sign loss in convergent Newton–Schulz inversion of Stieltjes matrices
